verdict.rationale: The Comptroller documents two transacting channels for software: Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) for high-volume filers, and electronic franchise-report submission through approved tax-preparation provider software, which implies a vendor/transmitter program. The evidence does not show how a system account or provider enrolls, and the open-data SODA rail is read-only, so it does not count toward transacting. Missing for 10: a published enrollment/registration path for EDI or software providers, technical specs for the EDI or transmitter channel, documented system/service accounts, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a legal-ops lead, a documented system-to-system channel exists for software to transact with the service (system accounts, transmitter programs, batch providers), with the enrollment path published

citations.quote: Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) is for businesses with a large number of outlets, leases, schedules or authorities.
Texas Franchise reports may be submitted electronically with approved tax preparation provider software.
